content: 1. Omaveloxolone and Lopinavir Interaction: Lopinavir increases the plasma levels and effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for its metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor the patient closely for adverse effects and discontinue treatment if necessary. 2. Ritonavir and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of ombitasvir, paritaprevir, and ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely for toxicity. 3. Lopinavir and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir/Dasabuvir Interaction: Lopinavir increases the levels and effects of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. If unavoidable, monitor closely for increased paritaprevir levels and associated toxicity. 4. Ritonavir and Omeprazole Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 5. Ritonavir and Ondansetron Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration in patients with congenital long QT syndrome, electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure, or bradyarrhythmias. ECG monitoring is recommended. 6. Lopinavir and Ondansetron Interaction: Lopinavir increases the levels and effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Orlistat and Ritonavir Interaction: Orlistat decreases the levels and effects of ritonavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently in HIV-infected patients, as virological control may be lost. If an increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 8. Ritonavir and Osilodrostat Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 9. Lopinavir and Osimertinib Interaction: Lopinavir increases the levels and effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 10. Ritonavir and Ospemifene Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir can either increase or decrease ospemifene levels depending on the metabolic pathway affected. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 11. Oxaliplatin and Lopinavir Interaction: Oxaliplatin increases the levels and effects of lopinavir through mechanisms not fully understood. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Oxcarbazepine and Ritonavir Interaction: Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels and effects of ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 13. Ritonavir and Oxycodone Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Ritonavir and Ozanimod Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of ozanimod by inhibiting CYP2C8 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs. Monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 15. Ritonavir and Paclitaxel Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and toxicity of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor paclitaxel levels and toxicity closely. 16. Lopinavir and Pacritinib Interaction: Lopinavir increases the levels and effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Ritonavir and Palbociclib Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 18. Ritonavir and Pexidartinib Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 19. Phenobarbital and Ritonavir Interaction: Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 20. Ritonavir and Pimavanserin Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administered, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 21. Ritonavir and Pimozide Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of pimozide by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious adverse effects. 22. Ritonavir and Pioglitazone Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Ritonavir and Pirtobrutinib Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Ritonavir and Perampanel Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 25. Ritonavir and Paricalcitol Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor the patient closely for signs of increased toxicity. 26. Ritonavir and Paroxetine Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of paroxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 27. Ritonavir and Pasireotide Interaction: Ritonavir and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 28. Ritonavir and Pazopanib Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 29. Ritonavir and Peginterferon Alpha-2b Interaction: Peginterferon alpha-2b may alter the therapeutic effects of CYP2D6 substrates. Use caution when co-administering with antiretroviral protease inhibitors, as both can cause hepatic damage. 30. Ritonavir and Pemigatinib Interaction: Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. This detailed explanation provides a professional and precise understanding of the drug interactions.
